verdict: These are the same page — same 62ch measure, same 622px left edge, paper two greys apart out of 255 — so the argument is decided on smaller things, and B loses them. B buys 2px of extra leading (76 vs 74) and then spends 160px of vertical on a filename bar and a hairline-ruled '188 words 961 characters' counter, showing 16 text rows where A shows 18; a live word count parked under the last line is the first thing a drafting writer turns off. And B's headings step 26 and 52px right of the body edge, so the left margin ripples exactly where the page should feel most solid. A's failing is real but quieter: the hanging markers drag the ink 47px left of window centre with nothing to answer them on the right.

states.name: narrow
states.gap: Zero bottom gutter: the text column runs to the pixel edge of the window — the last list line is guillotined at y=1799 with only 4px of glyph tops showing and 0px padding below it, where B keeps 50px (25 CSS px) of clear paper above its divider. Type at the end of the file in A and your caret line sits flush against the window edge with nothing beneath it.
states.gapTheirs: The left margin is not a straight line: B sets the `#`/`##` inside the column, so H1 text starts 52px (26 CSS px) and H2 text 78px (39 CSS px) right of the body's left edge at x=142, while A hangs the markers into the margin and lands every heading and every body line on one ruled edge at x=181. Two visible steps in the margin per screen.
states.verdict: A is a page; B is a document window with a page inside it. B spends a 60px title bar and a footer band on chrome, then narrows the margins to 71/78 CSS px against A's 90/99 and stretches the measure to 63 characters against A's 57 — the column is closer to both edges, the lines are longer, and the left edge stutters right at every heading. A's one real sin is that it forgot the bottom: the column has no closing gutter and slices a line in half at the window edge, which is exactly what you'd feel typing the last paragraph of a chapter. Still A — a straight left margin, a 57ch measure and no live character counter in the eyeline beat a tidy footer.

states.name: short
states.gap: Line pitch 74px vs A's 76px (37 vs 38 CSS px, ~1.63 vs ~1.70 leading) on identical ~22.5px type, and the measure wraps three characters earlier (58–59 chars vs A's 62) — a marginally tighter, more crowded column.
states.gapTheirs: The heading's words start at x=673 while every body line starts at x=623 — the '#' occupies a cell inside the column instead of hanging, so the title is kicked 51px (~25 CSS px, two character cells) right of the prose and the page has no single flush-left axis; with an H2/H3 present that indent stair-steps further.
states.verdict: Two near-identical pages, and the whole decision is one vertical line: B holds a single left edge at x=623 for title and body alike, A lets the '#' eat a cell and shoves the title 51px inboard, so the eye trips on the one edge an empty page has nothing to hide. A buys back 2px of leading and three characters of measure — real, but you need a ruler to see it, whereas A's broken axis is visible from across the desk. Neither page does anything with the bottom 55% of the window: text is nailed to the top, first baseline at 75–77 CSS px, no vertical centering and no hint of typewriter scrolling, so both will feel like writing at the ceiling. B, on the axis alone.
